ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{2}{3x}$, there is a moving point A. Connect AO and extend it to intersect another branch of the graph at point B. In the fourth quadrant, there is a point C, satisfying $AC=BC$. As point A moves, point C always moves on the graph of the function $y=\frac{k}{x}$. If $\tan\angle CAB=3$, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OC, and draw AE $\perp$ y-axis at point E, and draw CF $\perp$ x-axis at point F, as shown in the diagram.\\
Due to the symmetry of line AB and the inverse function $y=\frac{2}{3x}$, points A and B are symmetrical about point O,\\
$\therefore$ AO = BO,\\
Also, since AC = BC,\\
$\therefore$ CO $\perp$ AB.\\
Since $\angle$AOE + $\angle$AOF = $90^\circ$, and $\angle$AOF + $\angle$COF = $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOE = $\angle$COF,\\
Also, since $\angle$AEO = $\angle$CFO = $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOE \sim \triangle COF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{CF} = \frac{OE}{OF} = \frac{OA}{OC}$,\\
Since $\tan \angle$CAB = $\frac{OC}{OA}$ = 3,\\
$\therefore$ CF = 3AE, OF = 3OE,\\
Also, since AE$\cdot$OE = $\left|\frac{2}{3}\right|$ = $\frac{2}{3}$, CF$\cdot$OF = $|k|$,\\
$\therefore$ |k| = 6,\\
$\therefore$ k = $\pm$6,\\
Since point C is in the fourth quadrant,\\
$\therefore$ k = \boxed{-6}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: [First describe the image] In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, and the curve is the two branches of an inverse proportional function: one branch is in the first quadrant, and the other branch is in the third quadrant. Point A is on the curve in the first quadrant. Connect A with the origin O and extend it, intersecting the curve in the third quadrant at point B; therefore A, O, and B are three collinear points and O is in the middle. There is point C in the fourth quadrant, and line segments AC and BC are drawn. [Then reason] Suppose A is on the function y=2/(3x), and is in the first quadrant. Let A=(a, 2/(3a)), where a>0. Denote b=2/(3a), then A=(a,b) and ab=2/3. The line AO passes through the origin O and intersects the other branch of the hyperbola at B. Since the function y=2/(3x) is centrally symmetric about the origin, and B is on the same straight line AO as A and is on the other branch, it can be obtained that B is the symmetric point of A with respect to O: B=(-a,-b). Given AC=BC, this shows that C is on the perpendicular bisector of AB. The midpoint of line segment AB is ( (a+(-a))/2, (b+(-b))/2 )=(0,0)=O, so the perpendicular bisector passes through O, and OC ⟂ AB. Also because AB and AO are collinear, OC ⟂ AO. Therefore the vector OA=(a,b), and a direction vector perpendicular to it can be taken as (b,-a). Point C is in the fourth quadrant, take C=t(b,-a), and let t>0 (at this time x_C=tb>0, y_C=-ta<0, indeed in the fourth quadrant). Thus |OC|=t|OA|. Next use tan∠CAB=3. Because AB and AO are collinear, ∠CAB is equal to ∠CAO. Also because OC ⟂ OA, triangle AOC is right-angled at O, so in right triangle AOC: tan∠CAO = (opposite side OC)/(adjacent side OA) = |OC|/|OA| = t. It is known that tan∠CAB=3, namely t=3. Therefore C=(3b,-3a). If C is always on y=k/x, then k=x_C y_C=(3b)(-3a)=-9ab=-9*(2/3)=-6.
